parts.text:
15 A measuring cylinder contains 80 cm3 of a liquid.
The pressure due to the liquid at the 60 cm3 mark is 1200 Pa.
What is the pressure due to the liquid at the base of the measuring cylinder?
A
1200 Pa
B
1600 Pa
C
3600 Pa
D
4800 Pa

hints: Notice the liquid surface is at $80\text{ cm}^3$, so find the volume of liquid above the $60\text{ cm}^3$ mark by doing $80 - 60$.
Recall $p = h\rho g$ for liquid pressure, so for the same liquid in a uniform cylinder pressure is proportional to depth $h$ and to volume above the point.
Compare the volume above the base, $80\text{ cm}^3$, with the volume above the $60\text{ cm}^3$ mark and scale the $1200\text{ Pa}$ by that ratio.
walkthrough: The cylinder has uniform cross-section, so depth $h$ below the surface is proportional to the volume of liquid above that level.
Surface is at $80\text{ cm}^3$. At the $60\text{ cm}^3$ mark the volume above is $80 - 60 = 20\text{ cm}^3$. Call its depth $h_1$.
Liquid pressure follows $p = h\rho g$, so with constant $\rho$ and $g$, $p$ is proportional to $h$. Hence $1200\text{ Pa}$ corresponds to $h_1$.
At the base the volume above is the full $80\text{ cm}^3$. Call its depth $h_2$. The ratio is $h_2/h_1 = 80/20 = 4$.
Therefore $p_{base} = 4 \times 1200\text{ Pa} = 4800\text{ Pa}$ with pressure in $\text{Pa}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: 1200 Pa is the pressure only $20\text{ cm}^3$ below the surface, not the full depth to the base.

B.explanation: 1600 Pa would follow from using the ratio $80/60$, which incorrectly uses volumes measured from the bottom instead of depth below the surface.

C.explanation: 3600 Pa is $3$ times 1200 Pa and does not match the correct $80$ to $20$ depth ratio for this uniform cylinder.

D.explanation: The depth at the base is 4 times the depth at the $60\text{ cm}^3$ mark, so pressure is $4 \times 1200\text{ Pa} = 4800\text{ Pa}$.
